model.title: To amend the Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act to support nucleic acid screening, and for other purposes.

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act
This bill explicitly requires the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to support the development of best practices and technical standards for nucleic acid synthesis.

Nucleic acids, including deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA), carry genetic information within cells. Nucleic acid synthesis is the process of designing and creating custom nucleic acids; it is used in the development of medications and agricultural products. However, this technology also poses a risk of misuse (e.g., the intentional or unintentional creation of dangerous biological agents).

The bill requires NIST to carry out measurement research to support the development and improvement of biosecurity best practices and technical standards related to nucleic acid synthesis. This effort must address specified topics including nucleic acid synthesis screening, operational security, and conformity assessment. (A 2023 executive order titled Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence directed NIST to develop and refine similar specifications and best practices for use by synthetic nucleic acid providers. NIST's work on this topic is ongoing.)

In carrying out this effort, NIST must convene stakeholders to develop and periodically update consensus priorities and best practices for synthetic nucleic acid screening mechanisms. Within a specified period, NIST must submit a summary of the stakeholder group’s findings to Congress.

NIST must also take steps to advance risk management best practices and technical standards for engineering biology and biomanufacturing, including with respect to risks associated with the use of artificial intelligence.

The Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act would require the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to help develop best practices and technical standards for nucleic acid synthesis. Nucleic acids, such as DNA and RNA, carry genetic information in living cells. Custom-making them is useful for medicines and farm products, but it also carries a risk of misuse, such as the creation of dangerous biological agents, whether on purpose or by accident.

To address this, NIST would carry out measurement research to improve biosecurity practices and standards in this area. The work must cover specified topics, including screening of nucleic acid synthesis, operational security, and conformity assessment. This builds on a 2023 executive order on artificial intelligence, which had already directed NIST to develop similar standards for companies that provide synthetic nucleic acids. NIST's work on this is still ongoing.

NIST would also bring stakeholders together to agree on priorities and best practices for screening synthetic nucleic acids, and to update them periodically. Within a set period, NIST must send Congress a summary of what this stakeholder group has found.

Finally, NIST would take steps to advance risk management practices and technical standards for engineering biology and biomanufacturing. This includes addressing risks linked to the use of artificial intelligence.
